definition: Instant noodles are pre-cooked and dried wheat noodles designed for quick preparation, usually sold with seasoning packets and commonly consumed as an affordable fast meal. They provide mainly quick energy from refined carbohydrates and added fats, but have limited overall micronutrient density compared to whole foods. A standard portion is 100 g of dry noodles, which provides approximately 520 kcal, along with around 52 g carbohydrates, 10.3 g protein, 31.7 g fat, 1.9 g fiber, and about 378 mg sodium. They are useful for fast energy and convenience, but should ideally be balanced with vegetables or protein sources to improve nutritional quality.
ingredients: Instant noodles are typically made from refined wheat flour, water, and vegetable oil (often palm oil), along with salt and food additives for texture and preservation, and they are usually served with a seasoning packet containing salt, spices, flavor enhancers, and sometimes dehydrated vegetables or artificial flavors.
